did: builder.py: added `import re` for the fence/heading patterns.

builder.py: replaced `strip_comments` with `_scan_line`/`note_text`, which remove `%%` comments while keeping `%%` inside a code span (per-line backtick runs) and inside a fenced block as the note's text, and raise ValueError when a comment is left open to the end of the note.

builder.py: replaced the old `fence` toggle with `opening_fence`/`closing_fence`, so a fence is three-or-more backticks/tildes indented at most three spaces and closes only on the same character with at least as many marks (four backticks hold three whole, a backtick block holds tildes).
builder.py: replaced `heading_level` with `heading`, which recognizes ATX headings indented at most three spaces; a line indented four is no heading and stays in the section.
builder.py: rewrote `goal_section` to find `## Goal` and end at the next level-1/2 heading while skipping fenced blocks in both scans.
builder.py: added `committed_file`, which uses `git ls-tree HEAD -- <path>` and accepts only modes starting `100`, so a directory, symlink or submodule entry is no seed whatever its bytes say.
builder.py: `read_seed` now rejects a non-regular commit entry via `committed_file` and reads the note through `note_text` before `goal_section`.
AGENTS.md: verified unchanged; it already states that the next seeds' builds are run with the seed's path, so the goal's AGENTS.md clause was already satisfied.
unsure: Whether edge cases not covered by the tests, such as a fence opener appearing after a `%%` comment closes mid-line, are intended to open a fence; I chose to treat only whole lines outside comments as fence openers.
